title: Does Corporate Tax Planning Affect Firm Productivity?
authors: Spyridon Gkikopoulos; Edward Lee; Konstantinos Stathopoulos
department: accounting (per abstract: accepted by Suraj Srinivasan)
near_miss_reason: Additional additive event-time fixed effects in every column. Table 4 (new banking relationship, NBR, design) estimates reghdfe av_tfp_op i.treat##i.post, absorb(g_b im5-im2 ip0-ip4 fyear): firm-bank FE, calendar-year FE AND relative-event-time FE (im5..ip4) for all firm-bank pairs, which the Nov 1 2026 ruling treats as an additional additive FE that makes the column ineligible; 'post' and 'treat' main effects are dropped as collinear with these FE. Columns 2-3 and 5-6 further add 3-year-average time-varying controls (av_vsize av_foinc av_tq av_rnoa av_capex av_rde av_fcf av_lev av_wwscore av_nol av_dnol) and columns 3 and 6 replace year FE with industry-year FE. Column 1 without the event-time FE would be an eligible static TWFE. The Check-the-Box design (Table 5) has a single adoption date (1997) and is not a staggered design.
eligible_reason: A staggered binary design exists: D = treat x post switches on at the firm-bank-specific start year of a new loan contract (minstart_fyear, spanning fiscal years 1993-2017, so many cohorts) for pairs whose lead bank is a 'tax-planning intermediary' (treat=1), with treat=0 new borrowers from other banks as controls (D=0 throughout) in a [-5,+4] event window; unit = firm-bank pair (g_b), time = fyear, cluster g_b (cols 1-3) or sic3 (cols 4-6). It is not eligible as reported because every column includes relative-time fixed effects, and most add time-varying controls. Lead should also rule on the comparison group: control pairs experience their own loan event (post=1) but are coded untreated, so the design nets out a common event-time profile rather than comparing to units without an event.
design_notes: 09a_NBR_Identification_Strategy.do: builds firm-bank panel from cfubp.dta merged with data_dealscan_cleaned.dta; Indicator (bank is tax-planning intermediary: other borrowers' average CETR above median in >=3 of 5 pre-years); treat = max(status) over the pair (status = Indicator for new borrowers); post = fyear >= minstart_fyear; rel_time = fyear - minstart_fyear kept in [-5,4]; event-time dummies im5..ip4; outcome av_tfp_op = 3-year backward average of Olley-Pakes TFP (normalized). Table 4 cols 1-6 at lines 196, 208, 215, 228, 233, 239; dynamic DD (dd_m5..dd_p4 with controls) at line 266 feeds Figure 1. Tables D.1-D.4 repeat with alternative outcomes/samples (Online Appendix). 10a_CTB_Identification_Strategy.do: Table 5 single-date DiD (post = fyear>=1997, treat = firms with foreign income), firm FE + year FE (+ controls, industry-year FE). Published Table 4: treat x post = 0.033 (0.007), 0.022 (0.005), 0.018 (0.005); 38,925 firm-bank-years, 6,078 firm-bank pairs; cols 4-6 same coefficients with SE 0.006/0.005/0.005 clustered on 187 industries.
estimators_reported: TWFE static DiD with event-time FE (reghdfe, Table 4)
main_or_robustness: robustness (Section 4.4 identification strategy; headline results are OLS associations)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Loan-start years span fiscal years 1993-2017 (fyear FE has 25 categories in the log); exact cohort counts require the licensed DealScan/Compustat data.
never_treated_note: Control firm-bank pairs (treat=0) have D=0 in all periods but experience their own loan-start event.
